title: React with TypeScript: Quick Revision Handbook
summary: Night-before revision notes for typing React components in TypeScript: props, children, state, events and generics. Also covers Vite setup, hooks lint rules, and debugging with React DevTools and the Profiler.

chapters.title: Typing Props and Children
points: Props are typed with an interface or type alias on the destructured parameter: function Card({ title, count = 0 }: CardProps). Annotate the parameter instead of using React.FC.
Optional props use ?, and defaults go in destructuring. Required props missing at the call site fail at compile time.
children is typed as React.ReactNode, which covers strings, numbers, elements, arrays, null and fragments. React.ReactElement accepts only a JSX element, so it is stricter.
Extend native element props with React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'> (or extends it in the interface) so a wrapper forwards onClick, disabled and the rest via ...rest.
Common mistakes: typing children as JSX.Element (rejects strings and null), using any for props, and passing a function prop without a signature such as onSelect: (id: string) => void.

chapters.title: Typing State and Events
points: useState infers the type from its initial value: useState(0) is number. Write useState<User | null>(null) when the initial value is narrower than the real type.
Arrays and empty objects need an explicit generic: useState<string[]>([]), otherwise the type is never[].
Event handlers use React types: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> for inputs, React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement> for clicks, React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement> for submit.
Inline handlers infer the event type from context. Only a handler defined separately needs the explicit event type. Use React.ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> to type the whole function.

useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null) gives a ref whose .current may be null, so check it before use. Since @types/react 19 every RefObject has a writable .current; it was read-only in 18. useReducer takes a discriminated union of actions so the switch narrows each case.

chapters.title: Generic Components
points: A generic component declares a type parameter: function List<T>({ items, render }: { items: T[]; render: (item: T) => React.ReactNode }). T is inferred from the items passed in.
Constrain with extends so the component can rely on fields: <T extends { id: string }> lets you use item.id as the key.
In a .tsx file, a bare arrow generic <T> parses as JSX. Write <T,> or <T extends unknown>, or use a function declaration.
Generic hooks pass the type through: function useFetch<T>(url: string) returns { data: T | null }, and the caller sets it with useFetch<User[]>('/api/users').
React.memo and forwardRef erase generics. Cast the result or use a function declaration wrapper to keep T.

chapters.title: Vite Project Setup
points: Create a project with npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts. Then run npm install and npm run dev.
Scripts: dev starts the server with HMR, build runs tsc then vite build into dist/, and preview serves the built output locally.
Env vars must be prefixed VITE_ and are read through import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL. Unprefixed variables are not exposed to client code.

vite.config.ts uses defineConfig with the react plugin. A dev server proxy (server.proxy) forwards /api to the backend and avoids CORS in development. The @ alias needs both resolve.alias in Vite and paths in tsconfig.

Vite does not type-check during dev, because Vite's transform only strips types. Run tsc --noEmit or rely on the build script to catch type errors. Entry is index.html at the project root, not in public/.

chapters.title: ESLint Rules for Hooks and DevTools
points: eslint-plugin-react-hooks provides two rules: rules-of-hooks (error) and exhaustive-deps (warn). Enable both with the plugin's recommended config.
rules-of-hooks: call hooks only at the top level of a component or custom hook. Never inside conditions, loops, nested functions or after an early return. Custom hook names must start with use.

exhaustive-deps flags any reactive value used in useEffect, useCallback or useMemo that is missing from the dependency array. Fix the code (move the function inside the effect, or wrap it in useCallback) instead of disabling the rule.
React DevTools Components tab: inspect props, state and hooks of any component, edit values live, and use the search box to find components by name.

Profiler tab: record an interaction, then read the flamegraph and ranked chart. Gray bars did not render and colored bars did. Enable 'Record why each component rendered' to see changed props, state or hooks, and use Highlight updates to spot needless re-renders.

chapters.title: React TypeScript Cheat Sheet
points: Props: interface Props { title: string; children?: React.ReactNode; onSelect: (id: string) => void }
State: useState<User | null>(null), useState<string[]>([]), useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
Events: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>, MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>, FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>
Generics: <T extends { id: string }> constraint, and <T,> in .tsx arrow functions

Vite: npm create vite@latest app -- --template react-ts, env vars need the VITE_ prefix, and tsc --noEmit does the type-check. Hooks: rules-of-hooks plus exhaustive-deps, and Profiler with 'Record why each component rendered'.
